data.name: Charmian
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Charis, meaning 'grace, beauty, charm'. In Greek mythology, Charis was a goddess of charm and beauty. In the New Testament, the Greek word charis is translated as 'grace' or 'favor'.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine grace and favor bestowed upon us.
data.numerology_meaning: People with the life path number 2 are compassionate, diplomatic, and peaceful. They are often drawn to the arts, and are natural mediators and healers.

in_hebrew.name: כָּרְמִיָּן
in_hebrew.meaning: שם מקורו מאור, אור, גאוה, חן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם הנשים שמקורו באור, גאוה, חן. השם כבר מופיע בתלמוד, וככל הנראה יש קשר לשם הנביא שלמה ששמו יפה. בספר תולדות, שמואל, הקרוי גם 'עז' שבאנגלית - 'Charmian', שמואל האח, היה רופא, סופר, ואגדה. ייתכן שהשם 'Charmian' קשור ל'charme' (צרפתית) - 'שם' (fr), 'Charm' (צרפתית).

in_greek.name: Χαρμίαν
in_greek.meaning: όνομα που προέρχεται από την απελευθερωτική και ευχάριστη φύση
in_greek.long_meaning: όνομα που προέρχεται από την απελευθερωτική και ευχάριστη φύση. Αναφέρεται σε ένα πρόσωπο που έχει την ικανότητα να προσελκύει και να συντροφεύει. Ονομάζεται έτσι επειδή είναι μια χάρη του Θεού. Στον Νέο Testamento, το όνομα 'Χαρμίαν' δεν αναφέρεται.

in_latin.name: Charmian
in_latin.meaning: nomen femininum originem habet ex lumine, delectatione, charmate
in_latin.long_meaning: nomen femininum, originem habens ex lumine, delectatione, charmate. In historia Ecclesiae, nomen 'Charmian' invenitur in nomine S. Samuele, fratris S. Samuele magi, qui fuit medicus, scriba, fabulator. Hoc nomen potuit provenire a vocabulo 'charme' in lingua Gallica - 'nomen' in lingua Francica, 'Charm' in lingua Gallica.

in_english.name: Charmian
in_english.meaning: name originating from light, joy, and charm
in_english.long_meaning: name originating from light, joy, and charm. Refers to a person who has the ability to attract and befriend. Named thus because it is a gift of God. In Christian tradition, the name 'Charmian' is associated with Saint Samuel, the brother of Saint Samuel the Magician, who was a physician, scribe, and fabulist. This name may have originated from the word 'charm' in French - 'name' in English, 'Charm' in French.

saint_reference.note: brother of Saint Samuel the Magician, a physician, scribe, and fabulist
